besluite.fout: 'steenkool water' runs together and can be misread as one noun group on a first reading.
besluite.rede: Adding the article makes the object of 'kook' clear without changing who heats what, and leaves the protected 'hitte' intact.

besluite.fout: The comma between the fronted comparison and the inverted verb copies an English pattern and reads stiffly.
besluite.rede: Starting with the subject and setting the comparison off reads more naturally, with the same plants, the same action and the same comparison.

besluite.fout: 'miljoene jare gevat om te vorm' copies English 'took millions of years to form'.
besluite.rede: 'oor miljoene jare gevorm' says the same duration in natural Afrikaans and matches the lesson's own phrasing, and the next sentence's contrast still holds.

besluite.fout: An existential sentence with an indefinite subject ('baie plante') lacks the 'daar' Afrikaans naturally uses.
besluite.rede: Adding 'daar' makes the sentence read naturally without adding or moving any meaning.
